:::{#exm-empirical-cdf}
#### Numerical example: empirical CDF

Suppose the observed values are $4, 1, 7, 3$, so $n = 4$.
Two of the four values (1 and 3) are at most 3.5, so:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hat F(3.5)
&= \frac{1}{4}\paren{I(4 \le 3.5) + I(1 \le 3.5) + I(7 \le 3.5) + I(3 \le 3.5)}
&& \text{(definition of $\hat F$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{4}(0 + 1 + 0 + 1)
&& \text{(evaluate each indicator)}\\
&= 0.5
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, $\hat F(0) = 0$, because no value is at most 0,
and $\hat F(7) = 1$, because every value is at most 7.
:::
